newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open $5 to $10 higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open $5 to $10 higher.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $5 to $10 higher Monday as traders expect the market to bounce back after Friday's weak close.

Traders said CFTC's Commitments of Traders report released late Friday was supportive. The data showed speculators (non-commercials and nonreportables) were net long some 25,000 lots as of June 17, which was toward the lower end of traders expectations of a 25,000 to 35,000-lot speculative net long position.

New York cocoa futures ended sharply lower Friday on speculative profit taking. September settled down $26 at $1,613 a tonne after ranging between $1,638 and $1,611. Spot July ended $29 lower at $1,566, while the back months finished down $20 to $28.
Technically, traders pegged September support at $1,596. On the upside, resistance was seen at $1,630, then $1,638-$1,640.
CFTC reported non-commercial long positions in the two weeks ended June 17 rose by 5,769 lots, to 22,138 lots. Non-commercial short positions fell by 1,126 lots, to 3,142 lots.
Commercial long positions in the two weeks fell by 4,445 lots, to 56,632 lots, while commercial short positions rose by 3,039 lots, to 82,093 lots.
Nonreportable longs positions increased by 642 lots, to 16,700 lots and nonreportable short positions increased by 53 lots, tp 10,235 lots.
In London, cocoa futures were barely changed in light trade early Monday. LIFFE September was up one stg at the midday break, to 1,112 stg, while spot July was flat, at 1,093 stg.
